operator_io_quirks: All identifiers double-quoted in DDL; FK clauses use backticks (`Artist_ID`) — sqlite_master text mixes quoting styles; keep original DDL verbatim.
Table/column names are mixed-case (Artist_ID, Year_Join, Ticket_Price); column lookup must be case-insensitive, output keeps original spelling.
Tiny tables (7/6/13 rows) — original_values lists are complete, no rowid sampling needed; original_sizes must still be full count(*).
exhibition_record has composite PK (Exhibition_ID, Date) — both members are composite-PK members, so max_l0=30 for both samplers.
Date column is TEXT storing 'December 2' style (month-name, no year, no zero-pad) — declared type TEXT dispatches to String fuzzer, NOT Date; TS will never produce this format.
Year_Join and Year are INT but semantically years (1988-2008, 2004-2008) — Number fuzzer will emit values in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from INT args (none) => default scale, wildly off.
Ticket_Price REAL with 2-decimal values (19.95 etc.) — Number float fuzzer perturbs by ±0.01/±0.02, plausible; but fresh draws uniform over full range.
FK exhibition.Artist_ID -> artist.Artist_ID: parent has 7 rows, child 6, parent_exists true, parent PK unique — clean FK, no dangling.
FK exhibition_record.Exhibition_ID -> exhibition.Exhibition_ID: parent 6 rows, child 13 rows => child FK values drawn with replacement, duplicates expected (fine, not unique).
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints anywhere — only PKs; insert failures will be rare (PK dupes only).
No self-references, no missing parents, no non-unique parents, no storage-class/declared-type contradictions (all integer->INT, text->TEXT, real->REAL).
No views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs; DDL clone is trivial.
operator_ts_expectations: artist.Artist_ID, exhibition.Exhibition_ID, exhibition_record.Exhibition_ID: Number fuzzer, int, no args => scale default, fresh draws uniform over huge range then ±1/±2 perturbation; PK dedup keeps first occurrence.

artist.Name, Country, exhibition.Theme: String fuzzer, length range from min/max element len (Name ~9-11, Theme up to ~40), CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9(), 50% contaminate — produces gibberish names, not real country/theme strings.

exhibition_record.Date: String fuzzer (declared TEXT) — will emit random strings like 'aB3()', never 'December 2'; any query filtering Date by month name or LIKE 'December%' will see implausible values => likely FN (gold rows not matched) or FP (spurious matches).

Year_Join, Year: Number int fuzzer — fresh draws uniform over [-10^scale,10^scale] (scale from INT with no args => default), so years like 1998 become e.g. 4839201 or -77; range predicates (Year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010) will mostly return empty or wrong sets => FN/FP.
Age: Number int, original 45-57; fresh draws far outside => age filters implausible.
Ticket_Price: Number float, scale from REAL (no args) => default; fresh uniform over full range, perturb ±0.01/±0.02; price comparisons (Ticket_Price < 20) may flip.
Attendance: Number int, original 965-2983; fresh draws huge => attendance thresholds implausible.

FK consistency: exhibition.Artist_ID drawn from artist.Artist_ID final values (7 distinct) with replacement; exhibition_record.Exhibition_ID from exhibition.Exhibition_ID (6) with replacement — joins preserved structurally, but parent PKs may be perturbed so join cardinality shifts.
Composite PK (Exhibition_ID, Date) dedup: with random Date strings, collisions unlikely => 13 rows survive; but if Date sampler reuses elements (max_l0=30) duplicates possible => row drops.
p=0.2 default, 30% chance whole-instance p=0 => sometimes all values are original elements (perturbed), sometimes mostly fresh — bimodal quality.
No Date/Time/Bool fuzzers triggered on this DB (no date/timestamp/bool/bit/year declared types) — the text-stored dates are the main quality gap.
Small tables mean TS sizes (30-2500) vastly exceed originals => many duplicate PKs dropped, final row counts unpredictable but small.
